using a white VW Gol in the Jardim das Palmeiras neighbourhood. Officers
found the car, but the driver tried to flee when he saw the patrol car and was
caught after a pursuit lasting several blocks. A joint Military Police and
Civil Police task force then found two other suspects at a snack bar. Those
involved were taken to the Água Clara Civil Police station for legal procedures.

marijuana-like substance totalling about 54 kilograms.

Sul, after the report about sales in Jardim das Palmeiras. Police said the
seizure should help the investigation into the suspects' alleged drug dealing in

report.body:
Mossos d'Esquadra officers of the DIC detained seven men aged 29 to 55 on 1
October on suspicion of belonging to a drug-trafficking organisation. The
operation took place in an industrial warehouse in Cabanes, in Girona, where
officers seized 8,025 kg of hashish. Officers entered the building and
found seven people unloading pallets from the trailer intending to move the
hashish into different vans for later distribution. The seven detainees
were brought before the Civil and Instruction Section of the Figueres Court of
Instance.

The hashish was hidden among legal cargo inside large raffia sacks filled with
rubber crumb, a system used to hinder detection at police or customs checks. Police valued the seized substance at more than 16.2 million euros on the
illicit market. The seizure accounts for a significant share of the hashish
seized by the Mossos in 2026, with nearly 14,900 kg seized up to 1 October.

The investigation had begun in June 2026 after officers intercepted a van
carrying nearly 2,400 kg of hashish in Viladecans, which investigators linked to
the Cabanes warehouse. Surveillance found only sporadic entries of people
and vehicles with no business activity visible, alongside apparent loading and
unloading movements. Officers also found a firearm in one of the detainees'
vans. The almost entirely open-plan premises showed no sign of business or
residential use. The investigation remains open and further arrests or
actions have not been ruled out.

report.body:
Spain's UDYCO drug unit arrested a truck driver at the port of Ceuta carrying a
stash of hashish hidden in a sophisticated false bottom. Officers
intercepted the truck on the port road at the Muelle de Poniente and searched it
with support from the UPR prevention unit and the canine group. They found
the hashish and detained the driver, showing him the drugs found in the vehicle
he was driving.

The truck appeared empty and was heading toward boarding for Spain when a
specialist drugs dog alerted, prompting an exhaustive hours-long search inside
and outside the vehicle. After the hours-long detailed inspection, officers
found a large number of bags full of hashish inside the truck's structure.
Officers recovered numerous bags of hashish from the trailer's false bottom,
with first estimates putting the haul above 300 kilograms although police gave
no official weight. The submitted account describes the seizure as about
300 kilograms of hashish arriving from Morocco.

The handcuffed driver was taken to police headquarters and placed under
investigation for an offence against public health. On Sunday the driver was brought before a judicial authority, which ordered his remand in preventive prison for an offence against public health. Police link the
operation to open UDYCO investigations into groups moving hashish from Ceuta to
mainland Spain in heavy vehicles with hidden compartments. The investigation remained open over suspected larger loads and heavy vehicles hidden in spaces used as hashish stores.

National Police in Palma arrested four men and a woman suspected of belonging to
a group dedicated to drug trafficking. Group I of the Narcotics unit said
the arrests closed an investigation begun months earlier, with five people
detained in total. The inquiry began after officers learned of a hashish
parcel addressed to a man living in Palma.

Officers intercepted the parcel, found it held 24 kilos of hashish and arrested
its recipient on suspicion of drug trafficking. The investigation then
pointed to other suspected collaborators and two homes where more drugs might be
held. Officers searched both homes with support from prevention, drugs and
canine units. In the main suspect's home officers found 36 kilos of
hashish, an air rifle fitted with a silencer and around 10,000 euros in cash. A man and a woman were arrested there as suspected perpetrators of drug

the total hashish seized at 60 kilos, 24 kilos from the parcel and 36 kilos from
the house.

Investigators arrested another suspect who was allegedly responsible for storing
and transporting drugs and searched his home. That search found 2 kilos of
cocaine plus further doses, cutting agents, a pistol with 9-millimetre
cartridges, a bow with arrows and a hydraulic press allegedly used to compress
cocaine. Officers arrested a fifth person in connection with the case.
Police suspect the drugs were to be passed to third parties for smaller-scale

Immigration police raided a luxury three-storey rental house on Khu Bon 27 in
Bang Khen district, Bangkok, on 19 October 2026. The search was conducted
under a warrant issued by the Min Buri Criminal Court. Officers acted after
nearby residents complained about a strong lingering smell of cannabis.

Bangkok. The offence of processing or selling cannabis without proper local
authorisation carries up to one year in prison or a 20,000-baht fine.

Thai national who originally rented the property to find the masterminds behind

substation, with the assistance of the KC-HIDTA task force and the Taft Police

Mexico on cultivation, marijuana-for-sale, conspiracy and delaying or
obstructing allegations and booked him into the Taft jail facility.

During the search, deputies eradicated a total of 660 marijuana plants.
Deputies also found dangerous pesticides within the grow site.

The Sheriff's Office said the Taft substation deputies were assisted by the
KC-HIDTA task force and the Taft Police Department. The investigation was
described as active and ongoing, with no court outcome reported beyond the
arrest and booking.
